exposure: antenatal placement of occlusive balloons in the uterine arteries
surgeon experience (dedicated experienced surgeon vs. not)
cohort: Women who underwent postpartum hysterectomy at the Jewish General Hospital, McGill University, between 1992 and 2011 (n=67)
finding: While overall rates of postpartum hysterectomy increased over the study period, this was primarily due to an increase in planned procedures for placental abnormalities, with a decrease in unplanned emergency hysterectomies.
mod_finding: The risk of requiring a massive blood transfusion was increased when postpartum hysterectomy was performed after vaginal delivery compared to cesarean section.
